headline: Connecticut activates emergency operations center for nor’easter
dek: The state moved into partial activation Saturday as officials warned of strong winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding through the weekend.
body: Connecticut activated its Emergency Operations Center ahead of a nor’easter expected to bring heavy rain and strong winds across the state, Gov. Ned Lamont’s office said.

The center entered enhanced monitoring mode at 10 p.m. Friday and partial activation at 7 a.m. Saturday. State agency staff and partner liaisons are providing in-person support, with a virtual component for additional partners to share real-time information. The center is expected to remain active around the clock for the duration of the storm.

The governor’s office said the National Weather Service had issued wind advisories for all of Connecticut through Sunday morning. Coastal flood warnings were in effect for Fairfield and New Haven counties, while advisories covered Middlesex and New London counties through Sunday evening.

State emergency managers said they had held coordination calls with every municipality. Lamont urged residents to follow updated alerts, avoid flooded roads and prepare for the possibility that strong winds could bring down trees and limbs, block roads and cause power outages.

Road conditions are available through CTroads.org, and residents can subscribe to the state’s CT Alert system. The emergency-center activation coordinates information and resources; it does not by itself declare a statewide state of emergency.
author: NorthEast News Desk
